title: Canonical section tensor and proper projection comparison data
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and the native Weil-sheaf framework and ambient derived tensor of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] and [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$, let $R$ be a normalized coefficient realization and $S$ its ordinary section-module closed structure as in [lem-sf-adic-qbar-constructible-realization]. Define $U_0$ to be actual Frobenius forgetting (the native forgetful functor of [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models]) followed by the section-module functor, $U_{Ch}$ its termwise cochain functor, and $U$ the corresponding exact derived functor, with its canonical localization-factor isomorphism. A section tensor comparison is a cochain isomorphism $U_{Ch}\operatorname{Tot}_W(P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}_S(U_{Ch}P,U_{Ch}Q)$ on every pair of native complexes, equal to the identity on each left-first homogeneous pure balanced tensor summand, together with preservation of K-flatness and a derived tensor isomorphism $U(A\otimes_W^LB)\cong UA\otimes_S^LUB$. The latter is normalized by the actual total-complex comparison and the K-flat model isomorphisms, summand insertions, sheaf tensor and pullback of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-operations], with the conventions of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-presentation-data]. Both totals use left degree first and differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_Q$; no exchange of bidegrees or factors is implicit. This is comparison data for the closed forgetful realization of [lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful], not its existence theorem. For a morphism $p_0:Z_0\to Y_0$ between separated finite-type schemes, define the native projection source and target functors using the actual native tensor, pullback and right-derived direct image, and the actual cochain-to-derived pushforward computation map. Using the adjunction of [lem-sf-derived-weil-pullback-pushforward-adjunction], the balanced comparison data of [def-sf-native-projection-tensor-comparison-data], and the ordinary operations of [lem-sf-adic-proper-adjunction-realization], define the ordinary and common-stage projection arrows as their actual counit mates; the common-stage arrow uses the canonical common-stage pullback/tensor comparison of [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. The common-stage arrow has the proper identity-open normalization. Also define the termwise comparison induced by any specified sheaf direct-image comparison. No invertibility of a projection arrow is asserted.
